title: A regional rail operator's 25-kilovolt alternating-current electrified network uses 150-square-millimetre copper-silver
user_text: A regional rail operator's 25-kilovolt alternating-current electrified network uses 150-square-millimetre copper-silver overhead contact wire suspended at 20 kilonewtons tension with staggered steady arms every 60 metres, and pantograph contact strips wear the wire unevenly: at 300-metre-radius curves and near level crossings where trains brake heavily with the pantograph still raised, localized wear flats and hard spots deepen to the 25-percent wear limit while straight sections stay below 10 percent, forcing speed restrictions to 40 kilometres per hour and emergency wire replacements at roughly 60,000 euros per possession on the worst 8 kilometres of route each year. Sparking at the worn hard spots also degrades the pantograph carbon strips prematurely, doubling strip consumption on the commuter fleet. We need localized wear on curved and braking sections held below the 25-percent renewal limit for at least 15 years of service on the existing wire, without converting the route to a different overhead system, without lowering line speed below the current 120 kilometres per hour on straight sections, and without re-tensioning the entire wire in one possession.
